speaker: I. M. Gelfand
title: Elementary analysis exercises and rapidly oscillating integrals
summary: Four numbered exercises precede Beilinson's heading: Thomae's function and its powers, a double-limit representation of the Dirichlet function, the obstruction to a single limit of continuous functions, and Fourier integrals with quadratic, quartic, and sextic decay. These are definite questions with classical solutions, not evidence of newly announced unresolved conjectures.

speaker: A. A. Beilinson
title: Inverse and direct images of D-modules
summary: The manuscript heading on the lower part of P000937 begins this talk, following I. M. Gelfand's exercises. Beilinson constructs ordinary inverse images of left modules and transfer bimodules for direct images of right modules, tests them on point inclusions and delta modules, and introduces derived integration and its de Rham interpretation. The actual continuation reaches P000939, beyond the catalogue range. P000936 belongs to the preceding meeting.

speaker: S. I. Gelfand
title: Two exercises on derived categories
summary: The upper portion of P000940, before the explicit 24 November heading, gives an exercise separating isomorphic cohomology from a chain map and an incompletely specified dual-sphere equivalence. The latter does not determine a kernel, an equivariance convention, or a precise category; its resemblance to a Radon transform is insufficient for an exact identification.

speaker: D. B. Fuchs
title: Whitehead products and the Jacobi identity
summary: A short intervention gives the boundary-of-a-product construction of the Whitehead product and its graded Jacobi identity. The target homotopy degree is one too high in the manuscript itself; this is a faithful mathematical error, not an English translation error.

speaker: V. I. Lomonosov
title: A compressed perturbation statement for commuting operators
summary: The manuscript records a trace-class difference for two operators, a compact difference for another pair, two commutation assertions, and a claimed unitary equivalence of absolutely continuous restrictions. The primes and the operators used in the spectral subspaces do not yield a valid identifiable theorem as written. A standard scattering-theoretic repair can be proved, but is explicitly separated from any attribution to Lomonosov.

speaker: A. A. Beilinson
title: Derived direct images and holonomic modules
summary: The talk starts below the Fuchs and Lomonosov interventions on P000940 and continues through P000943. It treats composition of derived direct images, Spencer and relative de Rham complexes, Gauss--Manin connections, closed embeddings, point-fibre criteria for holonomicity, finite length, and simple modules as minimal extensions of irreducible connections. Several assertions need the distinction between a closed embedding and an arbitrary locally closed embedding.

title: YEAR 1981
summary: This catalogue record is a calendar-year divider before the 9 February MacPherson talk. No independent mathematical assertion belongs to it, so it has no occurrence-index items. The actual P000949 scan begins with the date and MacPherson heading; the catalogue divider is not represented as a separate manuscript theorem or talk. Adjacent Novikov and MacPherson material is assigned to their own manuscript headings.

speaker: Robert D. MacPherson
title: Grassmannian simplices, the dilogarithm, and convexity
summary: The talk, described as joint work with I. M. Gelfand, develops positive diagonal-torus orbit closures in real Grassmannians, hypersimplex combinatorics, cross-ratios, Pontryagin-form integration, and a five-term dilogarithm identity. It then reports Atiyah's extensions to Kähler and symplectic geometry. The unrestricted harmonic-form assertion, the use of an orbit in place of an orbit closure, and the final Hamiltonian-orbit diagram each need distinct qualifications. The construction continues the 1979 occurrences 1979-486.12--15 and 1979-487.1--2.

speaker: A. G. Khovanskii
title: Newton polygons, genus, mixed volumes, and toric compactification
summary: Khovanskii explains how Newton polygons determine the genus and punctures of a nondegenerate curve, derives root counts through boundary valuations, introduces mixed area, and connects Pick's formula and Minkowski's inequality with toric intersection theory. The notes cite his 1977 and 1978 papers and Danilov's 1978 survey. P000960 starts the 23 February meeting, so it is not part of this lecture despite the catalogue endpoint.

speaker: A. G. Khovanskii
title: Continuation: monomial charts and fans
summary: This recovered catalogue record continues Khovanskii after the Cherednik and Gelfand interventions of 23 February. The live catalogue's decade typo had excluded it from the supplied academic-year list. Character--cocharacter pairings, cones of one-parameter subgroups, a modification chart, the completeness criterion, and the fan of the projective plane precede the separate Kazarnovskii heading. The actual manuscript date is 1981, not 1991.

speaker: B. Ya. Kazarnovskii
title: Zeros of exponential sums and mixed pseudovolume
summary: Kazarnovskii extends Newton-polytope root counting to exponential sums with complex spectra, explains mixed pseudovolume through faces and complex tangent geometry, and mentions its support-function formulation. A separately dated 2 March question by I. M. Gelfand asks for the connection with the growth indicatrix; that follow-up is included with its own speaker and date, while the neighbouring Gaussian-tail exercise is assigned to record 514.
